description: Intent i008 (error-unwind-poisoned-count, snapshot s02) complete. Reported finding: fs/dlm/member.c:118-128 dlm_slots_copy_in() — peer-controlled count with no local clamp, consumed by an OOB in-place read-modify-write loop, with asymmetric sibling validation. Evidence chain from s02 source: (1) Poisoning store into shared kernel state: member.c:118 'num_slots = le16_to_cpu(rf->rf_num_slots);' with only 'if (!num_slots) return -1' — no maximum, no cross-check against the peer-supplied h_length or ci_buffer_size. The rf_num_slots field comes from a remote DLM cluster node's rcom_config recovery message copied verbatim into the persistent shared ls->ls_recover_buf (kmalloc(dlm_config.ci_buffer_size), lockspace.c:586) by receive_sync_reply() at rcom.c:266 'memcpy(ls->ls_recover_buf, rc_in, rc_in->rc_header.h_length);', consumed after wait_status_low() via dlm_recover_members() (recover.c:208). (2) Validation gap: midcomms.c:78-101 validates only the declared total length h_length (>= sizeof(dlm_rcom), <= ci_buffer_size, <= received len) — never the embedded slot count. (3) Asymmetric validation: the sibling transmit path dlm_slots_assign() enforces 'max_slots = (ci_buffer_size - sizeof(struct dlm_rcom) - sizeof(struct rcom_config)) / sizeof(struct rcom_slot); if (num > max_slots) ... return -1;' (member.c:276-281), but the copy_in/receive mirror path has no such clamp — the seed's submit-vs-return asymmetry. (4) Unsafe use: member.c:124-127 walks ro0 for num_slots iterations (16-byte rcom_slot each, dlm_internal.h:487-492) performing in-place 'ro->ro_nodeid = le32_to_cpu(ro->ro_nodeid); ro->ro_slot = le16_to_cpu(ro->ro_slot);' — up to 65535 iterations (~1MB) of OOB read+write past the heap ls_recover_buf; log_slots (member.c:129, loop at 86) and the matching loop at member.c:132-134 iterate the same unclamped count. (5) Error-unwind poisoning: early returns at member.c:141-144/152-155 leave ls->ls_generation updated from the peer (member.c:117) and member slots partially populated from the OOB walk, poisoning recovery state later stages consume. Confidence medium: the invariant violation (validated length, unvalidated count, no local maximum on the mirror path, enforcing sibling) is verified from source; exploitability needs a malicious/buggy cluster peer to send rf_num_slots exceeding the slot records its validated h_length carried — not reproduced at runtime (read-only snapshot, multi-node DLM required).
